clues.text: High hills shield it from the north and west. So this basin town stays mild, and folks call it the Nice of the North.
clues.narrowing: narrows to a mild, mountain-sheltered basin town on that river

source.quote: Its location in a mountain basin at the southern foot of the Taunus, protected by the mountains in the north and west, gives Wiesbaden a mild climate. It has been called the "Nice of the North" because of its climate and architecture.

source.quote: In 1806, the city became the capital of the Duchy of Nassau. Since 1841, the newly built Wiesbaden City Palace was the principal Nassauian residence.

clues.narrowing: near-decisive: an old spa town with many hot springs in its centre

source.quote: Wiesbaden is one of the oldest spa towns in Europe. Its name translates to "meadow baths", and there are 15 mineral springs—14 of which are hot springs—in the city centre.

clues.text: Each day its springs pour out two million liters of water. No spa town in all of Germany beats it but one.
clues.narrowing: converts: the second most productive spa town in Germany

source.quote: With a yield of around 2 million liters daily, Wiesbaden is the second-most productive German spa after Aachen.

clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside Aegean Turkey

source.quote: Denizli is a city in Aegean Turkey, and seat of the province of Denizli.

clues.narrowing: narrows to an inland Aegean town with hot summers and snowy winters

source.quote: The weather is hot in Denizli in summers, whereas in winters, it may occasionally be very cold with snow on the mountains that surround the city. Some years, snow can be observed in the urban areas.

source.quote: Denizli also attracts visitors to the nearby mineral-coated hillside hot spring of Pamukkale, and with red color thermal water spa hotels Karahayıt, just 5 kilometres (3 miles) north of Pamukkale.

source.quote: The city forms the urban part of the districts Merkezefendi and Pamukkale, with a population of 691 783 in 2024.
